status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is the single most significant finding of this audit: 'cancelled' is stale/wrong as the CURRENT status. Per the brief's guidance, dating each step from source: (1) 2012-02-22 -- Williams/Cabot announce the joint venture (SEC 8-K). (2) 2014 -- FERC issues the original certificate, 149 FERC PP61,199 (CP13-499). (3) 2016-02 -- tree-felling/construction begins in Susquehanna County, PA. (4) 2016-04-22 -- NY DEC DENIES the Clean Water Act Section 401 water-quality certification, the PIVOTAL document per the brief's own framing, holding that Constitution 'fails in a meaningful way to address the significant water resource impacts' (dailygazette.com, ogj.com, both directly confirming the date). (5) 2017-08-18 -- the 2nd Circuit upholds the DEC denial (Constitution Pipeline Co. v. Seggos; stateimpact.npr.org, per the wiki's own citation). (6) 2018-04-30 -- the US Supreme Court denies certiorari, exhausting the litigation (ecowatch.com/nrdc.org). (7) 2020-02-24 -- Williams and partners abandon the project, citing diminished risk-adjusted returns after $354M in write-downs (pgjonline.com, courthousenews.com/AP). (8) 2021-11-18 -- the original FERC certificate is vacated by the 2nd Circuit in a related proceeding (New York State Dep't of Envt. Conservation v. FERC, No. 19-4338 -- confirmed directly from the FERC petition PDF's own case history). (9) 2025-05 -- Williams signals intent to revive Constitution alongside NESE amid a Trump-administration/Hochul-administration deal (pgjonline.com, naturalgasintel.com, Bloomberg). (10) 2025-12-19 -- Constitution Pipeline Company, LLC formally PETITIONS FERC to reissue the lapsed certificate, explicitly invoking a 'waiver by inaction' theory that NY DEC forfeited its Clean Water Act authority by failing to act on a renewed 401 request within one year (the FERC waiver fight named in the brief). (11) 2026-01-08 -- FERC issues its Notice of Petition. (12) 2026-01/02 -- NY's Attorney General and DEC formally urge FERC to dismiss/reject the petition (marcellusdrilling.com, hoodline.com), and litigation opposing the revival is filed by environmental groups and NY DEC in parallel (marcellusdrilling.com, 2026-05). (13) 2026-08-21 -- FERC releases its Environmental Assessment, finding the project 'would not constitute a major federal action significantly affecting the quality of the human environment' -- i.e. FERC is proceeding toward reissuance over NY's objections. (14) 2026-08-26 -- Federal Register publishes notice of EA availability, comment period open through 2026-09-21 (today's date in this audit is 2026-09-10 -- the comment period is STILL OPEN). Given an active FERC docket, a completed favorable Environmental Assessment, a targeted 3Q2026 certificate reinstatement and a stated late-2027 in-service date (naturalgasintel.com), this project is squarely back in active development -- 'cancelled' materially understates its status. Recommend Status='proposed' (no ground has been broken under the reissued authority yet, and NY DEC/environmental groups are actively litigating to block it, so 'construction' would overstate it). CancelledYear=2020 should NOT be removed -- it remains historically accurate (see the Cancelled [ref] fill) -- but the live Status field should reflect the current, actively-contested revival rather than the 2020 abandonment. ShelvedCancelledType ('confirmed') likewise reflects the 2020 event accurately and needs no change regardless of the Status recommendation. | ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-14 CANCELLATION-FIELD CLEARING (slice-wide sweep 7(b), same ruling as P4070). A row cannot carry a live Status and a cancellation/shelving date at the same time: that pairing is the defect class this sweep exists to find, and it would misreport this project in every downstream count. Sheet carries CancelledYear=2020 and ShelvedCancelledType='confirmed' alongside the proposed Status='proposed'. Both are cleared. Constitution is a REVIVAL: Williams genuinely cancelled it in Feb 2020 and genuinely revived it in 2026 (Notice of Petition Jan 2026; FERC EA with FONSI Aug 2026, Federal Register 2026-17399). A revived project is not a cancelled one. NOTE ON DELIVERY: this row sits in `deepsweep-remainder`, which was already shipped as slice 1's CLOSED batch-5 workbook.
